### MTB — Earnings soften as expenses and credit costs rise

**Reported GAAP diluted EPS declined to $5.04 from $5.32 in 2Q26**, a $0.28 sequential miss. Net income available to common shareholders declined to $732 million from $781 million [B0020, B0021]. The bank also disclosed diluted net operating EPS of $5.08, a separate operating measure rather than a designated ex-notable-items EPS figure [B0287].

**Revenue and margin:** GAAP NII was broadly flat at $1,793 million versus $1,792 million. Headline NIM declined 5 basis points to 3.65%. Noninterest income increased modestly to $743 million, but noninterest expense rose $44 million to $1,393 million. The efficiency ratio deteriorated to 54.4% from 52.8% [B0013, B0033, B0017, B0018, B0034].

**Credit:** Provision increased to $135 million from $120 million. Net charge-offs rose to $127 million from $80 million, and the annualized charge-off ratio increased to 0.35% from 0.23%. The disclosed allowance-for-loan-losses ratio was 1.51%, but this is not a separately confirmed total ACL coverage ratio [B0016, B0126, B0127, B0036].

**Capital and returns:** CET1 was 10.16%, while annualized ROTCE was 17.29%. M&T repurchased $323 million of common shares [B0038, B0064, B0048].

**Outlook:** Fourth-quarter guidance called for $1.83–$1.85 billion of taxable-equivalent NII, $710–$730 million of fees and $1.39–$1.41 billion of GAAP expenses [B0784].

**Investment thesis:** Slightly negative near term. Capital and profitability remain substantial, but margin compression, higher expenses and rising charge-offs temper the outlook.
